claims.subject: Rellekka
claims.value: Of the teleports the Rellekka page lists, only Camelot Teleport (as a tablet) is usable by the owner today; the Slayer ring (Fremennik Slayer Dungeon) is a possible second option once 75 Slayer points are earned
claims.statement: The Rellekka page lists the teleports to the town. The owner cannot use these: Fremennik sea boots (need the easy Fremennik diary; owner has no diaries), the enchanted lyre (needs The Fremennik Trials), the ring of wealth Miscellania teleport (needs Throne of Miscellania), the eagle transport system (needs Eagles' Peak, not in the owner's quest list), the DKS fairy ring (excluded by dispatch), the Music cape (99), and a house teleport (the owner's house is in Rimmington, not Rellekka). Camelot Teleport works through the GE-tradeable tablet (C-LOG-077), but the page calls it 'a very long run south of the village'.

Docking at Rellekka needs 62 Sailing plus The Fremennik Trials (C-LOG-086 caveat). The lyre requirement is already settled in C-LOG-086.

claims.subject: Rellekka Rooftop Course
claims.value: Camelot tablet (lands 2757,3479) -> road north from Camelot -> left at the first fork towards Rellekka; optional 48-Agility log balance north of Sinclair Mansion
claims.statement: This is the owner's working route to the Rellekka course today. Break a Camelot teleport tablet (it lands at map square 2757,3479), then follow the road north from Camelot and take the left at the first fork towards Rellekka. The log balance north of Sinclair Mansion needs 48 Agility (owner has 57) and gives 'slightly faster travel' into the Fremennik Province. It has a success-chance chart, so it can be failed. The course is in Rellekka (map 2625,3677), with the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon to its east. The run's length in tiles or seconds is unknown, no source. The Rellekka page only calls it 'a very long run'.

sources.title: Fremennik Slayer Dungeon
sources.quote: *Players may teleport to [[Camelot]] and travel the road that leads north, taking a left at the first fork, which leads you towards Rellekka. There is a [[log balance (Fremennik Province)|log balance]] [[shortcut]] south-west of the cave, requiring 48 [[Agility]] to pass.

sources.title: Log balance (Fremennik Province)
sources.quote: The '''log balance''' is an [[Agility]] [[shortcut]] found in the [[Fremennik Province]], north of the Sinclair Mansion. An Agility level of 48 is required to use the shortcut. The shortcut provides slightly faster travel to the Fremennik Province.

claims.subject: Slayer ring
claims.value: lands just inside the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon (entrance 2797,3616, east of Rellekka); no requirement for this destination; ring is untradeable and costs 75 Slayer points; cave crawlers in chamber 1 are aggressive to combat 46 and below
claims.statement: The Slayer ring's Fremennik Slayer Dungeon teleport has no requirement and lands 'just inside the entrance' of the cave east of Rellekka. The cave page calls it the fastest way to the cave. From the cave you walk to Rellekka (the page describes the reverse trip: from Rellekka, head south-east past the Golden Apple Tree). The ring is untradeable and costs 75 Slayer points from a Slayer master. Points start only from the fifth task, and Turael/Spria tasks give none. A Porcine of Interest (completed by the owner) gave a one-time 30 points. The owner's current balance is unknown. HAZARD: the first chamber has cave crawlers, which are aggressive to combat level 46 and below. The owner is combat 45.

Teleports in the cave were not checked against the Wilderness or other restrictions; the cave is not in the Wilderness.

claims.subject: Rellekka Rooftop Course
claims.value: no bank in Rellekka; candidate full banks: Keldagrim (needs The Giant Dwarf started; via the tunnel east of Rellekka), Seers' Village bank (south end of the Camelot road), Barbarian Outpost bank chest (walking link to Rellekka not established); distances unknown, no source
claims.statement: Rellekka has no bank (C-LOG-087). The nearest full bank to the course is unknown, no source. Candidates: (1) Keldagrim bank, reached through the tunnel entrance east of Rellekka. Entry needs only to start The Giant Dwarf by talking to the Dwarven Boatman. Its skill requirements are not needed to start, and the owner meets them anyway (Crafting 21/12, Firemaking 30/16, Magic 44/33, Thieving 24/14). The wiki names Keldagrim as the nearest bank to the mine east of Rellekka (the other, Zanaris, needs fairy rings). (2) Seers' Village bank, at the start of the Seers' course and the south end of the Camelot road. (3) The Barbarian Outpost bank chest (games necklace teleport). No source gives a walking route from there to Rellekka; the Lighthouse page describes only basalt rocks north to the Lighthouse, where a slip deals up to 10 damage.

sources.title: Keldagrim
sources.quote: Travelling to Keldagrim requires starting [[The Giant Dwarf]] quest. The quest can be started by talking to the [[dwarven boatman]] just outside the city, in the cave north-east of [[Rellekka]].

sources.title: Keldagrim entrance mine
sources.quote: The mine is quite far from a [[bank]], with the nearest ones being in Keldagrim via a cave to the north, and [[Zanaris]] via the [[fairy ring]] ({{Fairycode|DKS}}) on the snowy hill to the north-east.

sources.title: Barbarian Outpost
sources.quote: The Barbarian Outpost bank chest is commonly used due to its proximity to the games necklace teleport.

sources.title: Lighthouse
sources.quote: Players can get there from the [[Barbarian Outpost]] by jumping across the northern [[basalt rock]]s that protrude from the sea. It is possible to slip on the rocks, which results in the player falling into the water, being swept back to shore, and taking up to 10 damage.

claims.notes: Medium because nearness is not measured. The Giant Dwarf's Firemaking 16, Magic 33 and Thieving 14 lines carry the same {{Questreqstart|no}} marker (lines 30-32 of rev 15375425). Hazards inside the Keldagrim tunnel and on the river crossing were not researched (Threat Analyst). Seers' bank location is settled in C-LOG-075.

claims.value: free teleport to the Blast Furnace in Keldagrim every 20 minutes once Keldagrim has been visited
claims.statement: Once the owner has visited Keldagrim, the free Minigame Teleport (all spellbooks, 20-minute cooldown, 11.4-15 s cast that combat interrupts) can go to the Blast Furnace in Keldagrim. This gives a free, repeatable way back to the Keldagrim side of the Rellekka area. Run time from Keldagrim to the Rellekka course: unknown, no source.

claims.subject: Camelot teleport (tablet)
claims.value: the Seers' Village destination is the hard Kandarin diary reward; no source shows the tablet's Seers' option working without it, so for the owner the tablet lands at Camelot
claims.statement: The Camelot tablet has right-click 'Camelot', 'Seers' Village' and 'Toggle' options. The Seers' Village (bank) destination is the hard Kandarin diary reward: 'Camelot Teleport can now be used to teleport to Seers' Village bank instead'. Jagex's 2015 patch note says Camelot tablets go to the new location 'if you have them set'. The 2018 note says tablets now offer 'either of their possible destinations'. Treat the Seers' option as needing the hard Kandarin diary, which the owner can never complete (C-QST-256). Plan on landing at Camelot. Seers' Village is just south-west of Camelot, which the wiki calls the closest teleport to the village.

claims.value: lands at the inside entrance of the Ape Atoll Dungeon (cave on the south of the island, map 2771,9102); using it requires FULL completion of Monkey Madness I
claims.statement: The Ape Atoll teleport tablet (GE-tradeable, no Magic level needed) lands at the inside entrance of the Ape Atoll Dungeon, a cave on the south of the island. The wiki calls it 'a safe location'. Using it requires completing Monkey Madness I. The course needs only partial completion up to Chapter 2 (C-QST-080), so the owner cannot use the tablet until the whole quest is done.

sources.title: Ape atoll teleport (tablet)

claims.subject: Ape Atoll Agility Course
claims.value: from the tablet: exit the dungeon and run north-west through the gates; alternatives: CLR fairy ring (excluded), standard Ape Atoll Teleport (Magic 64 + Freeing King Awowogei), gnome glider (Ape Atoll glider needs Monkey Madness II)
claims.statement: From the Ape Atoll tablet landing, exit the dungeon and run north-west to pass the gates to reach the course. The wiki lists the route options from fast to slow: the CLR fairy ring (excluded for the owner); the standard Ape Atoll Teleport (64 Magic plus Freeing King Awowogei; owner has 44 Magic), then run south; the Arceuus teleport or its tablet, then run north-west through the gates; or a gnome glider, but the Ape Atoll glider needs Monkey Madness II. Once Monkey Madness I is complete, the tablet is the owner's only teleport here. The route passes the gates, where monkey archers are aggressive without a greegree (C-THR-043). Wear the ninja greegree before leaving the dungeon.

The wiki says it is the only consumable that boosts Fletching consistently. The other listed Fletching boosts are out of reach: the Fletching cape (99), the bottle of suqah-free cola (untradeable, from a Lunar Sea crate that needs an eternal brazier on the boat), and the spicy stew (needs the Freeing Evil Dave part of Recipe for Disaster).

claims.subject: Thieving boost (+1 for Creature of Fenkenstrain)
claims.value: Bandit's brew (+1 Thieving, +1 Attack, drains Strength and Defence; GE-tradeable) is the usable option; spring sq'irkjuice needs Thieving 25 to obtain and is untradeable; spicy stew needs Freeing Evil Dave; Thieving cape needs 99; poison chalice see C-RFI-211
claims.statement: To reach Thieving 25 for Creature of Fenkenstrain (boostable; owner has 24, C-QST-093), the safe option is Bandit's brew. It is GE-tradeable, boosts Thieving and Attack by 1, heals 1 and drains Strength and Defence by floor(level x 6/100) + 3. For the owner that is Strength 32 -> 28. Defence is already 1. The other listed +1 Thieving boosts are out of reach: spring sq'irkjuice is untradeable and its garden needs Thieving 25 (circular), the spicy stew needs Freeing Evil Dave, and the Thieving cape needs 99. Do not use the poison chalice (C-RFI-211).

claims.value: 1/32 chance to take up to 49 damage (owner has 48 HP); only 9/32 chance of the +1 Thieving boost
claims.statement: HAZARD: the poison chalice is GE-tradeable and listed as a +1 Thieving boost, but only 9/32 (~28%) of drinks give it. One drink in 32 (~3.1%) deals 'up to 49 damage' and lowers Attack, Strength and Defence by 1-3. The owner has 48 Hitpoints, so a single drink could kill. Another 2/32 deal 5% of max HP. Do not route it on Hardcore Worlds.

claims.subject: Pool of Refreshment (Ferox Enclave)
claims.value: fully restores Hitpoints, Prayer and run energy; cures poison, venom and disease; resets ALL boosted or lowered skills; disables active prayers; no special attack restore at Ferox
claims.statement: The two Pools of Refreshment in the Ferox Enclave chapel fully restore Hitpoints, Prayer and run energy. They cure poison, venom and disease and reset every boosted or lowered skill. Drinking turns off active prayers. The Ferox pools do not restore special attack. Planners should note the reset: drinking removes an active summer-pie Agility boost.

sources.title: Pool of Refreshment
sources.quote: The '''pools of refreshment''' fully restore the player's [[hitpoints]], [[prayer points]], and [[Energy|run energy]]; cure [[poison]], [[venom]], and [[disease]]; and reset all [[Temporary skill boost|boosted]] or [[Temporary skill drain|lowered]] [[skills]]. Drinking from it will also disable all currently active [[prayer]]s.

sources.title: Pool of Refreshment
sources.quote: Two pools of refreshment are found in the chapel in [[Ferox Enclave]], as well as in the lobby area in [[Daimon's Crater]] for the [[Bounty Hunter]] minigame. The pools located in the enclave '''do not''' restore [[Special attacks|special attack]] energy, while the one in the crater does.

claims.notes: Daimon's Crater is the Bounty Hunter lobby; Bounty Hunter was disabled on Hardcore Worlds at launch (T1, Update:Hardcore Worlds Are Coming On November 4th rev 15379410 line 46), so that pool is not counted on.

claims.subject: Ferox Enclave
claims.value: PvP-safe town inside level 13-16 Wilderness; ring of dueling teleports directly into it without crossing the Wilderness; leaving through the barriers puts you in the PvP Wilderness, which Hardcore Worlds keeps
claims.statement: Ferox Enclave is a town in level 13-16 Wilderness where players cannot kill other players. A ring of dueling (GE-tradeable at 8 charges) teleports straight into it, so you reach the pool without crossing the Wilderness. The bank is a few tiles from the pool. The danger is outside the barriers. Hardcore Worlds keeps normal Wilderness PvP death rules, and Jagex calls its Wilderness 'even more dangerous than ever before'. Players who are tele-blocked cannot re-enter through the barriers, and while tele-blocked, players in their combat range can attack them in the semi-safe strip outside. Stay inside, and leave by teleport (level 13-16 is below the level-20 teleport limit, C-THR-035).

sources.title: Ferox Enclave
sources.quote: The town is a safe area within the Wilderness, meaning players cannot [[Player killing|kill other players]] while within the boundaries of the town. Due to the nature of the [[Tele Block]] spell, Ferox does not allow players who have had it cast on them to enter the town through the town's [[Barrier (Ferox Enclave)|barriers]] until the spell has worn off, though players may still enter whilst in combat.

sources.title: Ferox Enclave
sources.quote:
The level 13 [[Wilderness Obelisk|Wilderness obelisk]] is east of the Enclave. There are also a few safe methods of reaching Ferox Enclave that do not require players to traverse the Wilderness:
* A [[ring of dueling]] will teleport directly here.

sources.title: Ring of dueling
sources.quote: Furthermore, the [[Ferox Enclave]] teleport allows a player to use the [[Pool of Refreshment]] whilst gaining full health, prayer and run energy, although the Ferox Enclave teleport places the player slightly farther away from a bank chest.

sources.title: Update:Hardcore Worlds Are Coming On November 4th
sources.quote: For those of you PKing out there for added risk, death proceeds as normal in the Wilderness so you'll receive the same items you'd usually get in the main game. The Wilderness is even more dangerous than ever before, as you'll be making characters sit ''permanently''.

claims.notes: Medium: no Hardcore-Worlds-specific source confirms that Ferox's PvP safe zone behaves the same on HW worlds; the wiki page describes the main game. Ferox infobox: 'wilderness = 13–16', 'location = Wilderness (safezone)'. The Ferox page also lists Minigame Teleport to Bounty Hunter / LMS / Clan Wars; BH and LMS were disabled on HW at launch. Ring of dueling: exchange8 = Yes (only the full 8-charge ring is GE-tradeable). The Threat Analyst should rate the Wilderness exposure.

claims.subject: Seers' Village Rooftop Course
claims.value: church altar at the course end restores Prayer; Rapid Heal (Prayer 22; owner 44) doubles natural HP regen to 1 HP per 30 s
claims.statement: The Seers' course ends at Seers' Village church, which has an altar to restore Prayer. The course page suggests that players who keep failing keep Rapid Heal on all the time and recharge at that altar. Rapid Heal needs 22 Prayer (owner has 44). It doubles natural Hitpoints regeneration to 1 HP per 30 seconds and drains 1 Prayer point per 18 seconds. With a regen bracelet it gives 2 HP per 30 seconds.

sources.title: Seers' Village Rooftop Course
sources.quote: Players who are constantly failing obstacles can take advantage of the [[altar]] in the church at the end of the course by having the [[Rapid Heal]] [[prayer]] active at all times.

sources.title: Rapid Heal
sources.quote: '''Rapid Heal''' is a prayer unlocked at level 22 [[Prayer]]. Rapid Heal doubles the natural regeneration rate of the player's [[Hitpoints]] to 1 Hitpoint per 30 seconds instead of the natural rate of 1 Hitpoint per minute. This does not stack with the [[Hitpoints cape]] perk, but does stack with the [[regen bracelet]] to regenerate 2 Hitpoints per 30 seconds.

sources.title: Seers' Village
sources.quote: |A large church to Saradomin, with a graveyard popularly visited for its [[yew tree]]s. The church is at the end of the rooftop course. Within it is an [[altar]] to restore [[Prayer]] at, and a [[church organ]].

claims.notes: Rapid Heal infobox: drain 3.333, 'Drain: 1pt per 18s'. At 44 Prayer points a full prayer bar lasts about 44*18 = 792 s (~13 min) before re-praying, computed and ignoring prayer bonus. Rapid Heal is slow (2 HP/min). It suits small fail damage, not big hits.

claims.subject: Forester's Arms (Seers' Village)
claims.value: meat pie 16 coins (12 HP, 2 bites of 6), stew 20 coins (11 HP), unlimited stock
claims.statement: Forester's Arms, the Seers' Village pub, sells meat pies for 16 coins (12 HP in two bites of 6) and stew for 20 coins (11 HP), with unlimited stock. Each purchase needs some dialogue, so buying in bulk is slow. It is cheap HP restoration a short walk from the Seers' course, bought with coins, so the thin HW GE supply does not matter.

sources.title: Forester's Arms
sources.quote: In addition to [[beer]], the bartender sells [[meat pie]] for 16 coins and bowls of [[stew]] for 20 coins. These are good prices but there's a bit of dialogue to go through for each one bought, so it's rather slow if large quantities are wanted.

sources.title: Stew

The same page warns that the barcrawl Liverbane Ale lowers Attack/Defence/Fletching/Firemaking/Woodcutting by 6. Do not buy it by mistake.

claims.subject: Ardougne Rooftop Course
claims.value: Ardougne church (central East Ardougne) has an altar for Prayer, so Rapid Heal can be used; market bakery food is settled in C-LOG-066
claims.statement: For the Ardougne course, the church in central East Ardougne has an altar (praying there is an easy Ardougne Diary task), so the owner can recharge Prayer and use Rapid Heal (C-RFI-214). Food can be bought for coins at the market bakery stalls where the course starts (C-LOG-066). The distance from the church to the course start is unknown, no source.

sources.title: Ardougne church
sources.quote: Praying at the [[altar]] is an [[easy Ardougne Diary]] task.

sources.title: East Ardougne
sources.quote: The [[East Ardougne church]] is located in the centre of the region.

claims.notes: Medium: no Ardougne course page links the altar to the course. The owner reaches the Ardougne course only at 85-90 Agility, by which point fail damage is low (C-LOG-071: no fails from 95).

claims.subject: Teleport to House (spell and tablet)
claims.value: default lands INSIDE the house next to the exit portal; right-click 'Outside' (spell and tablet) or the house-settings toggle lands OUTSIDE by the Rimmington portal
claims.statement: Teleport to House (spell, Magic 40, owner 44) and the GE-tradeable teleport-to-house tablet land inside the player-owned house by default, next to the exit portal. Since 2 August 2018 both have right-click 'Inside' and 'Outside' options; the tablet also has 'Group'. Left-click follows the 'inside or outside' setting in house options. A POH death is unsafe on Hardcore Worlds (C-LOG-003, C-THR-013). Set house options to land Outside, and use right-click 'Outside', so you land by the Rimmington portal and never inside the house by accident. Since 30 Nov 2022 the default can also be set to Building Mode, which still lands inside the house.

sources.title: Teleport to House
sources.quote: '''Teleport to House''', also known as 'House Teleport', teleports the caster inside their [[player-owned house]], right next to the exit portal (or within the house), regardless of the 'location' of the house ([[Rimmington]], [[Taverley]], [[Brimhaven]], etc.).

sources.title: Update:Tournament World, Mobile Enhancements and Theatre of Blood Tweaks
sources.quote: The Teleport to House and Teleport to house tabs now have right-click options for you to teleport inside and outside of your house. The left-click option will continue to respect the option you have selected in your house settings menu.

sources.title: Teleport to house (tablet)
sources.quote: |options = Break, Inside, Outside, Group, Drop

sources.title: Portal (Player-owned house)
sources.quote: In the house options screen, players can choose whether the house teleports land the player in the house itself or outside the portal.

claims.notes: CONFLICT: the Teleport to House page says dying in a POH respawns you 'NOT lose any items'. That is main-game behaviour. On Hardcore Worlds a POH death is an official (run-ending) death (T1, settled C-LOG-003). Its suggestion to house-teleport to escape poison would put an HW player inside the POH, so use 'Outside'. The 30 Nov 2022 Building Mode toggle is from the same page's change log.

claims.subject: Rimmington house portal
claims.value: land at/outside the Rimmington portal: house teleport or tablet with 'Outside', Construction cape, Rimmington (redirected) tablet; the 'Enter' option on the portal puts you inside
claims.statement: These land at the Rimmington house portal, outside the house: Teleport to House or the house tablet with 'Outside' (C-RFI-217), the Construction cape (the owner has Construction 23, so not available), and the redirected 'Rimmington teleport' tablet. The redirection scroll comes only from Nightmare Zone, which is unsafe on Hardcore Worlds (C-LOG-079 family). These land inside the house: Teleport to House or the tablet with 'Inside' or a left-click default of inside or Building Mode, and the portal's own 'Enter', 'Build mode' and 'Friend's house' options. Other ways near Rimmington with no house: Ardougne Teleport to the docks, then a 30-coin boat to Rimmington; skills necklace to the Crafting Guild north of the village; balloon to the Crafting Guild.

sources.title: Rimmington
sources.quote:
* {{Plink|Construct. cape|txt=Construction cape}} or {{Plink|Rimmington teleport}} — Rimmington house portal.
* {{Plink|Ardougne Teleport}} — Ardougne docks, which offer a trip to Rimmington for 30 [[coins]].
* {{Plink|Skills necklace}} can teleport players to the [[Crafting Guild]] north of the village.

sources.title: Portal (Player-owned house)
sources.quote:
*Enter your own house (only works if your house is in the same location as the portal)
*Enter your own house in building mode (only works if your house is in the same location as the portal)

sources.title: Teleport to house (tablet)
sources.quote: |change = The Nightmare Zone reward shop now sells Scrolls of Redirection that can be used to change the destination of a 'Teleport to House' tablet. You can choose a destination of any player-owned house portal, or Trollheim.

claims.notes: The Rimmington page also lists 'Teleport to Boat' to the Rimmington mooring point (needs 18 Sailing and a docked boat with a greater teleport focus). It lands at the mooring point, not the portal, and was not researched further. The owner's house location (Rimmington) comes from the dispatch, not from a game source.

Hardcore Worlds GE availability and prices for dragonfruit pies, Bandit's brew, rings of dueling, Ape Atoll and Camelot tablets: only main-game proxies exist; supply may be thin on new worlds.

limitations: All sources are OSRS Wiki pages pinned by revid plus three T1 Update: pages; no in-game verification. Wiki pages describe the main game; Hardcore-Worlds-specific behaviour is confirmed only where the T1 HW announcement speaks.
